hook.question: Guess: a slim South Asian woman and a slim white woman. How much higher is her diabetes risk?

reveals.label: higher diabetes risk
reveals.sentence: South Asian women aged 45 and over in Chennai, Delhi and Karachi with BMI under 25 kg/m2 had 5.3 times higher diabetes risk than US white women.

qualifiers: Adults aged 45 and over in Chennai, Delhi and Karachi, compared with US cohorts.
hook.quote: Similarly, in women, the risk of diabetes in those with BMI <25 kg/m2 was 5.3 times higher in South Asian (IRR (95% CI) 5.27 (3.64 to 7.54)) than in white women.

source.full: Narayan KMV, Kondal D, Daya N et al. Incidence and pathophysiology of diabetes in South Asian adults living in India and Pakistan compared with US blacks and whites. BMJ Open Diabetes Research & Care, 2021.

rounds.question: After stopping a weight management medicine, how long until weight is back where it would have been?

stops.label: About a year and a half

reveals.label: weight was no different
reveals.sentence: Across 28 randomised controlled trials, weight was no different between treatment and control groups 1.4 years after weight management medication stopped.

qualifiers: An average across studies, not a prediction for you.
rounds.quote: Among 28 randomised controlled trials, weight was no different between treatment and control groups 1.4 years after cessation of WMM.

source.full: West S, Scragg J, Aveyard P et al. Weight regain after cessation of medication for weight management: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ, 2026.

rounds.question: On these medicines, does lean mass go up or down?

reveals.label: Absolute lean mass fell
reveals.sentence: Absolute lean mass fell by 1.74 kg on average.

reveals.label: Lean mass as a share of total weight rose
reveals.sentence: Lean mass as a share of total weight rose by 1.81% on average.

qualifiers: Results varied a lot between studies.
rounds.quote: (layout sample only: not a usable claim yet)

source.full: Laverde et al. GLP-1 receptor agonists and lean mass: systematic review and meta-analysis. International Journal of Obesity, 2026.
